result:
task: Make `test_schema_clean_record` in `tests/unit/check/test_check.py` give its project the kernel's schema files, so a clean task record still gives no finding (DEC-746 item 1, P-A).
status: DONE — committed as `5aff5f6d`; `tests/unit/check` 99 passed; `tests/unit` 2108 passed, 1 skipped. The record's frontmatter also changed, which is one step past the decision's exact wording (see proposed_decisions).
work_completed: Added `_copy_kernel_schemas(root, *names)`, a small helper that only `test_schema_clean_record` uses. It copies the named single files from `template/governance/kernel/schemas/` in this repository into the test project at the same path (`template/governance/kernel/schemas/`), which is the first layout in `SCHEMA_DIRS` in `src/gov/check/schema.py:15`. The test now copies `ticket.schema.json` and `common.schema.json`. Copying the schemas alone did not make the test pass: the kernel's `ticket.schema.json` requires `role`, `allowed_paths` and `kpis`, and the old record had none of them, so `check` returned 3 `SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD` findings. I added those three fields to the test's record (`role: engineer`, `allowed_paths: [src/**]`, `kpis: {success: [it works], failure: []}`) so that it is a clean task record under the kernel schema. The assertion is still `check(root) == []`. No other test or shared helper changed, and no other file changed.
files_changed: tests/unit/check/test_check.py
evidence: Pre-flight: `printenv` → `product-spec`, `DAEO-zflj`; `git rev-parse` → `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-02`, `w2/W2-02`. `gov.__file__` → `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-02/src/gov/__init__.py`. Line removed: the old one-line record string.

discoveries: The decision expected the schema files alone to restore the test, but they don't. Once `ticket.schema.json` can be read, the old record (`id`, `type`, `status`, `state_class` only) is no longer clean: the kernel ticket schema requires `role`, `allowed_paths` and `kpis`. Before W2-02 the test passed only because the schema was never measured.
risks: Adding fields to the record goes beyond the decision's exact wording ("carry the kernel's schema files"), though it stays inside `test_schema_clean_record`. If the lead reads P-A strictly as "schema files only", this commit needs the lead's sign-off. The helper reads the schemas from this repository's `template/` at test time, so a later change to `ticket.schema.json`'s required fields will make this test fail too. That is intended, since the test should track the kernel.
lessons: Before deciding a fix for any "clean record" fixture under core-schema, check what the record's type schema requires. Making the schema readable also makes its required fields count.
proposed_decisions: PKG-1: confirm that P-A covers giving the record in `test_schema_clean_record` the three fields `ticket.schema.json` requires (`role`, `allowed_paths`, `kpis`), as committed in `5aff5f6d`. Recommendation: confirm (high confidence). The test keeps its purpose (a clean task record gives no finding), and its assertion and every other test are unchanged. The alternative is to assert the 3 `SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD` findings, but that changes the assertion, which P-A forbids, and turns this into a test of missing fields, which `test_schema_missing_fields` already covers.
unresolved: Owner or lead confirmation of PKG-1. DEC-746 is not yet in this worktree's register (it is named in no commit text).
recommended_next_action: Lead confirms PKG-1 and brings `5aff5f6d` into the W2-02 run-2 check.
